newsitem.title: USA: U.S. LPGs down as tide of Iraq crude approaches.
newsitem.headline: U.S. LPGs down as tide of Iraq crude approaches.

text.p: The U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas market was mostly down midday Friday, and traders said they expected prices to continue to slowly slip later in the day.
Belvieu propane was done about half-cent lower than Thursday at 36.725 cents a gallon, and traders said material would probably go lower.
Traders said they expect crude oil to fall next week, and, in turn, propane, as the United Nations continues to approve contracts for Iraqi crude in the oil-for-food deal.

The deal requires Iraq to export up to $1 billion in two seperate 90-day periods, the first one ending on September 5. Trading was thin in Belvieu butane as material slipped about a half cent. It was pegged at 43.75/44.25 cents. Belvieu isobutane was static.
Trading was thin in the Conway, Kansas market. Fourth-quarter propane sold at 37.63 cents, but few other deals were heard done.

"The NYMEX was up yesterday, and everyone thinks it will go up on Monday," said a Conway trader, "so people have already bought what their looking for." He said there were far more sellers than buyers.
